case.title: Teo’s Napkin Plan
case.hook: The boat parade is tonight, and Rosa’s cocoa cart is back on the boardwalk. But this year every outlet is taken by the parade stage. Rosa’s cousin Teo sketched a plan on a napkin: a bike on a stand that will run everything. Rosa wants proof.

notes: The bike spins a little generator (GEN).
It runs the lights, the menu sign AND the cocoa warmer.
FREE energy! It comes from nowhere!

reply.t: Free? Energy doesn’t come from nowhere. Where does it START, and how do we PROVE it?

stills.alt: A woman pedals a bike that stands on a trainer. It powers the speakers for a music stage on a town square.

case.question: Where does the energy for Teo’s pedal-powered cart really start, and what evidence proves it?
case.how: Find 4 clues as you work through the lesson. Then crack the case (solve it) at the top of the Assignment tab.

clues.t: A glow stick has no plug and no battery. Its light started as chemical energy stored inside. Energy doesn’t come from nowhere.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 1: the energy slot machine
clues.t: Every device has a starting and a resulting energy. A bike generator turns motion into electrical energy. A lamp turns electrical energy into light.
Evidence is something you can see, hear, feel or measure. “Teo says it works” is not evidence.

clues.where: The Lesson, Part 3: the card binder
clues.t: When you walk, chemical energy from your food becomes motion. Your body is an energy changer, too.

solve.title: Where does Teo’s “free” energy come from?
solve.q: Which answer fits all four clues?

options.t: It comes from nowhere. The generator makes new energy all by itself.
options.why: Check Clue 1. Energy doesn’t come from nowhere. Even a glow stick has a starting energy.

options.t: It starts as chemical energy in the rider’s food. Pedaling turns it into motion, the generator turns motion into electrical energy, and the lights turn that into light. The proof: the lights glow only while someone pedals.
options.why: Case cracked! Food → motion → electrical → light, and you can SEE the proof: stop pedaling and the lights go dark.

options.t: The string lights make their own light. The bike just keeps them company.
options.why: Check Clue 2. A lamp needs a starting energy: electrical. Where does that come from here?

options.t: Teo says it works, so that’s the proof.
options.why: Check Clue 3. Saying so is not evidence. Evidence is something you can see, hear, feel or measure.

glowstick.afterText: Crack one and look for clues.
glowstick.title: Crack a glow stick
todo: Bend it until it cracks: press Bend, or drag the ✋ up.
Tap the two things you really observe.

why.q: What is inside a glow stick?
why.t: Two liquids. One is sealed in a thin glass tube that floats inside the plastic tube. When the glass cracks, the liquids mix.

glowstick.dragHint: Or drag the ✋ up to bend it.
glowstick.crackLine: CRACK! The glass tube inside broke. Now the two liquids can mix.
glowstick.needBend: Bend it first, so the glass inside cracks.
glowstick.obsQ: What do you observe? Tap the TWO that really happen.

obs.t: I see a bright green color.

obs.miss: Touch a real one: it stays about as cool as the room. A glow stick makes light, not much heat.
Listen: after the crack, it makes no sound at all.

photo.alt: Two real glow sticks, one green and one blue, glowing in the dark.
photo.cap: Real glow sticks glowing in the dark. Photo: David Muelheims, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

glowstick.q: No plug and no battery. Where did the light’s starting energy come from?

opts.t: Chemical energy stored in the two liquids.
Nowhere. The light just appeared when I bent it.
opts.miss: Bending only broke the glass so the liquids could mix. Did the light start before or after they mixed?
Did it feel hot? A glow stick glows even sitting on a table.

glowstick.win: The glow stick’s light started as chemical energy. Nothing came from nowhere. Clue 1!

reels.afterText: dark roads turn it into heat you can feel
reels.title: The energy slot machine
todo: Pull the lever to get a device.
Stop the STARTING reel and the RESULTING reel on the right energy (or use ▲ ▼).
Press Check. A true line wins a card. Win all 5.

why.t: The first reel shows a device. You line up the energy it starts with and the energy it ends with. Only true lines pay out.

reels.needLever: Pull the lever first to get a device.

devices.why: Flip the switch and the bulb glows.
devices.missS: Where does a lamp get its energy? Follow the cord to the wall.

also.heat: True, a lamp gets a little warm. But what is its main job? Stop the reel on that.

devices.why: Your food powers your legs, and the wheels spin.
devices.missS: What gives YOUR legs energy? Think about breakfast.
devices.missR: What do the pedals and wheels do?

devices.why: Plug it in and you hear music.
devices.missS: A speaker needs a cord or a battery. What kind of energy comes through it?
devices.missR: What do you notice with your ears?

devices.missS: What hits a solar panel on a sunny day?
devices.missR: A solar panel can charge a battery. What kind of energy is that?

devices.why: Spin it, and it sends electricity down the wire.
devices.missS: A generator only works when something spins it. What kind of energy is spinning?
devices.missR: Teo’s generator sends energy down a wire to the lights. What kind?

reels.q: What does every winning line have?

opts.t: A starting energy that changes into a different resulting energy.
The same energy at both ends.
opts.miss: Look at your cards. Was any starting energy the same as its result?

opts.t: Energy that appears out of nowhere.
opts.miss: Every card had a starting energy. Look again.

reels.win: Every device starts with one energy and changes it into another. Clue 2!

bingo.title: Evidence bingo
todo: Press Play and watch Rosa’s cart.
The moment you see, hear, feel or measure something on your card, tap that square.
Get three in a row. One square never counts.

why.t: Each square is a piece of evidence. Tap it only WHILE it is happening in the scene. The scene loops, so you get more chances.

events.t: A warm mug in my hands

decoy.miss: Saying so is not evidence. You can’t see, hear, feel or measure it.

bingo.notNow: Not right now! Tap it WHILE it is happening.
bingo.needPlay: Press Play first, then watch the scene.
bingo.bingoLine: Every square you marked was something you could see, hear, feel or measure.

opts.t: You can see, hear, feel or measure it.

opts.miss: Could you ever mark the “Teo says” square?
Believing isn’t observing. What did every marked square have in common?

bingo.win: Evidence is what you can see, hear, feel or measure. Clue 3!

binder.afterText: Every card you finish goes into your binder.
binder.title: Fill the card binder
todo: Pick its starting energy and its resulting energy.
Pick the best evidence. A finished card shines and goes in your binder.

why.t: It shows that the energy CHANGED. “The lamp is tall” is true, but it doesn’t prove anything about energy.

cards.alt: A desk lamp glowing at night over a desk with a pencil cup.
cards.missS: What comes through the cord from the wall?
cards.missR: What do you see when it’s on?

ev.t: The bulb glows when I flip the switch.
The lamp is tall and bendy.
ev.miss: True, but does it show an energy change?

ev.t: My friend says lamps make light.
ev.miss: Saying so isn’t evidence. What can you observe?

cards.alt: A silver microwave oven with a number pad.
cards.missS: A microwave has a plug. What comes through it?
cards.missR: What happens to cold soup inside?

ev.t: Cold soup comes out steaming, and a thermometer reads hotter.
It has a door and buttons.
ev.miss: True, but does that show an energy change?

ev.t: It’s the newest one at the store.
ev.miss: That’s not something that shows energy changing.

cards.alt: Two people walking on a wooden boardwalk through a green Florida forest.
cards.missS: What gives your body energy? Think about lunch.

ev.t: My legs move, and I get farther down the boardwalk.

ev.miss: True maybe, but does it show an energy change?
That’s an opinion, not an observation.

cards.alt: Sunlight shining through a huge green taro leaf, showing its veins.
cards.missR: A leaf turns sunlight into stored food. What kind of energy is food?

ev.t: The plant grows new leaves when it gets sunlight.

ev.miss: True, but does green show an energy change?

cards.alt: Tall white wind turbines with three blades on a hillside under a blue sky.
cards.missR: Wires carry its energy to homes. What kind?

ev.t: When the blades spin, a meter shows electricity flowing to homes.

ev.miss: True, but does that show energy changing?

ev.t: The sign says it’s a wind farm.
ev.miss: A sign is someone saying so. What can you observe changing?

binder.credits: Photos via Wikimedia Commons: lamp, M. H. Mathias, CC BY 2.0 · microwave, Wrightmt, public domain · boardwalk, Everglades National Park, public domain · taro leaf, Avenue, CC BY-SA 3.0 · wind turbines, Joshua Winchell, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, public domain.
binder.q: Look at your “you walking” card. What is the starting energy for YOUR motion?

opts.t: Chemical energy from the food I ate.
Motion energy that was always in my legs.
opts.miss: Where did your legs get their energy? Check the card.

opts.t: Electrical energy from a wall outlet.
opts.miss: You don’t plug yourself in! Check the card.

binder.win: Your food’s chemical energy becomes your motion. Your body is an energy changer. Clue 4!

pedal.title: Pedal Teo’s bike
todo: Switch on the string lights, the menu sign and the radio.
Pedal: tap Left, Right, Left, Right (or the ← → keys). Then stop and watch.
Last, switch on the cocoa warmer.

why.t: A watt measures how fast energy is used. A strong grown-up rider can keep up about 100 watts for a while.

pedal.keysLine: Tap them one after the other, or press the ← and → keys after you tap the picture.
pedal.okLine: It works! Your pedaling powers everything that’s switched on.
pedal.lowLine: Not enough. Pedal faster, or switch something off.
pedal.stopLine: You stopped, and everything went dark. That’s evidence: the energy came from your pedaling.
pedal.ridersLine: The cocoa warmer needs about 1,500 watts. That’s about {n} strong riders pedaling hard at the same time!
pedal.bigLine: One rider can light the whole cart, but heating cocoa takes much more energy. Rosa will heat her cocoa at home and bring it in insulated jugs.
pedal.done: One rider lights the cart. The warmer needs a plug. And no pedaling means no light!

glowwake.title: The glowing wake
todo: Drag the boat across the dark water (or press Go).
Watch the water where the boat goes.

why.t: Yes! In Florida’s Indian River Lagoon, tiny comb jellies flash blue-green when a boat or a paddle stirs the water on winter nights. A comb jelly is not a jellyfish, and it can’t sting.

glowwake.dragHint: Or drag the boat across the water.

photo.alt: A see-through comb jelly with glowing rainbow-colored rows, swimming in dark water.
photo.cap: A real comb jelly (a sea walnut). The rainbow shine in this photo is aquarium light bouncing off its moving combs. Its own flash is blue-green, and you only see it in the dark. Photo: Steven G. Johnson, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

glowwake.q: The boat bumps the comb jellies, and they flash. What is the starting energy of the LIGHT?

opts.t: Chemical energy inside the comb jellies.
opts.why: Right! Like a glow stick, the jellies mix chemicals inside their bodies to make light. The bump only tells them when to flash.

opts.t: The boat’s motion turns straight into light.
opts.why: The bump is just the signal. Think about the glow stick: where did ITS light start?

opts.t: The Moon’s light bouncing off the water.
opts.why: The flashes happen only where the boat stirs the water. Moonlight is everywhere.

glowwake.win: Living glow sticks! Chemical energy → light.

glowwake.tease: A boat’s wake glows in the dark, with no lights at all. How?

hlCoach.title: Highlight like a scientist
tips: Highlight key words, not whole paragraphs.
If everything is yellow, nothing stands out. Aim for a few words in each paragraph.
Look for words that are explained.
Bold words, and words followed by “means”, “is called” or a meaning in ( ), are often worth saving.
Look for answers to the Big Question.
Ask yourself: does this help me say where the energy started, what it became, and how I know?
“Because”, “so” and “first … then” show how ideas connect.
Yellow = important. Green = evidence I might use in my answer. Pink = something I wonder about.

practice.q: Practice: tap the 3 to 5 words that matter most in this sentence.
practice.text: A great claim names the energy change and points to evidence you can see, hear, feel or measure.
practice.model: A scientist might highlight “claim”, “energy change” and “evidence”. Those words hold the big idea.

hlCoach.outside: This works in every subject. When you read anything, save the words that answer your question, and skip the rest.
